approach: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble, which has two surfaces, is balanced by the pressure of the oil column of the given height.

steps.text: Write the excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius R.
steps.why_this_step: A soap bubble has two free surfaces, an inner and an outer one, so its excess pressure is twice that of a single liquid surface.

steps.text: Write the pressure of the oil column of height h that balances this excess pressure.
Equate the two expressions and solve for the surface tension T.
steps.equation: 4T/R = ρ_oil g h  ⇒  T = ρ_oil g h R / 4

steps.text: Substitute the given values and evaluate.

common_mistakes.text: Using the excess pressure of a single free surface, 2T/R, instead of the soap bubble's two surfaces, 4T/R, gives 9×10⁻² N m⁻¹.
Mistaking the given 0.5 cm for the diameter and halving it again to 0.25 cm before using it as the radius gives 2.25×10⁻² N m⁻¹.
